section: Water pollution - sources, eutrophication, Namami Gange, sewage treatment, groundwater contamination (arsenic, fluoride)

accepted.s: The disease Minamata is associated with which pollutant and country-year combination?
accepted.x: Minamata disease was caused by methyl mercury contamination in Japan and was identified in 1956.
accepted.tq: Use the disease–pollutant–location–year association.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the principal environmental pathway involved in Minamata disease?
o: Nitrate reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of infant blood
Cadmium accumulates in bones through contaminated irrigation water
Methyl mercury biomagnifies through fish and causes neurological damage
accepted.x: Methyl mercury biomagnified in fish and caused neurological damage in Minamata disease. The other options describe fluorosis, blue baby syndrome and Itai-itai disease respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the mechanism to the disease rather than relying only on the disease name.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about fluorosis:
1. Dental fluorosis mainly affects children below eight years of age.
2. Knock-knee is a form of skeletal fluorosis.
3. Fluorosis may also have non-skeletal manifestations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dental fluorosis is associated particularly with children under eight, knock-knee is skeletal fluorosis, and fluorosis also has non-skeletal forms.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the classification of fluorosis.

accepted.s: Fluoride causes fluorosis principally by replacing which component in hydroxyapatite?
accepted.x: Fluoride replaces hydroxyl in hydroxyapatite and forms fluorapatite.
accepted.tq: Test the precise biochemical substitution rather than the broader disease association.

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations relating to fluoride standards and observance is correct?
o: WHO guideline: 0.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.0 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 5 June
WHO guideline: 1.0 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.5 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 9 September
WHO guideline: 1.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.0 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 9 September
WHO guideline: 1.5 mg/L; BIS acceptable limit: 1.5 mg/L; National Fluorosis Day: 13 September
accepted.x: The WHO limit is 1.5 mg/L, while the BIS acceptable limit is 1.0 mg/L; the permissible BIS limit is 1.5 mg/L. National Fluorosis Day is observed on 9 September.
accepted.tq: Split the option into linked numerical and date components.

accepted.s: The Nalgonda technique for defluoridation uses which combination of materials?
accepted.x: The Nalgonda technique uses alum, lime and bleaching powder to remove excess fluoride from water.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific treatment-material combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Arsenicosis — skin lesions and skin and lung cancer
Blue baby syndrome — methyl mercury biomagnification
accepted.x: Arsenicosis or blackfoot disease is associated with skin lesions and skin and lung cancer. The other pairings interchange the pollutants and diseases.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched disease–pollutant effect pair among confusable associations.

accepted.s: The blue baby syndrome associated with nitrate contamination is medically known as
accepted.x: Excess nitrate in drinking water can cause methaemoglobinaemia, commonly called blue baby syndrome, in infants.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the common name and the medical term.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Ganga conservation framework in chronological order:
A. National Ganga Council replaced NGRBA
B. Central Ganga Authority and GAP-I
C. NGRBA was constituted
D. NMCG was set up as the implementing arm of NGRBA
accepted.x: The sequence is 1985 Central Ganga Authority and GAP-I, 2009 NGRBA, 2011 NMCG, and 2016 National Ganga Council.
accepted.tq: Place the dated institutional milestones first and last before resolving the middle sequence.

accepted.s: Ganga Action Plan-II, launched in 1993, covered which group of rivers?
accepted.x: GAP-II covered the Yamuna, Gomti, Damodar and Mahananda rivers.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact river-group membership.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the institutional history of Ganga conservation is correct?
o: The NRCP was created in 1985 and GAP-I was merged into it in 1995.
The NGRBA was chaired by the Prime Minister and was replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016.
The NMCG replaced the National Ganga Council in 2011.
The Central Ganga Authority was established in 2016 as a registered society.
accepted.x: NGRBA, chaired by the Prime Minister, was replaced by the National Ganga Council in 2016. NMCG was set up in 2011 as a registered society and implementing arm of NGRBA.
accepted.tq: Use the authority–chairperson–replacement relationship to reject swapped institutional roles.

accepted.s: The National River Conservation Plan and Ganga Action Plan-II became linked in 1995 because
o: NRCP was merged into the National Ganga Council
GAP-II was merged into the NRCP
accepted.x: In 1995, GAP-II was merged into the National River Conservation Plan.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of institutional merger, a common APPSC trap.

accepted.s: The Namami Gange Mission was announced in 2014–15 with an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for
accepted.x: The original Namami Gange Mission had an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for five years, covering 2015–2020.
accepted.tq: Separate the original mission period from the later Phase-II period.

accepted.s: Namami Gange Mission is identified as a key policy priority towards achieving which Sustainable Development Goal?
accepted.x: Namami Gange is linked with SDG 6, which concerns clean water and sanitation.
accepted.tq: Match the programme objective with the correct SDG.

accepted.s: Namami Gange-II was approved in 2022 with an outlay of ₹22,500 crore for the period
accepted.x: Namami Gange-II was approved in 2022 with ₹22,500 crore for 2021–2026, up to 31 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Phase-II dates and outlay from the original mission figures.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs represents the twin goals of the Namami Gange Mission?
accepted.x: Nirmal Dhara denotes unpolluted flow, while Aviral Dhara denotes continuous flow.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the formal twin-goal terminology from related programme components.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Namami Gange Mission:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
2. It has received support from the World Bank.
3. Arth Ganga links livelihoods with the river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Namami Gange is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, has World Bank support, and Arth Ganga concerns river-linked livelihoods.
accepted.tq: Verify each institutional, financial and conceptual feature separately.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component or associated activity of the Namami Gange Mission?
o: Expansion of uranium mining along the river basin
accepted.x: Sewerage, river-surface cleaning, afforestation, biodiversity, riverfront development, industrial effluent monitoring, Ganga Gram and public awareness are associated with the mission; uranium mining is not.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the established programme-pillars group.

accepted.s: Which of the following outcomes is associated with the Namami Gange Mission?
o: A first dolphin estimate of 627 animals in March 2025
accepted.x: The reported outcomes include afforestation over 33,024 hectares. The programme also ranched 143.8 lakh carp fingerlings and estimated 6,327 dolphins in March 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate similarly presented outcome figures and units.

accepted.s: The first estimate of the Ganga river dolphin under the reported Namami Gange outcomes recorded how many dolphins in March 2025?
accepted.x: The first dolphin estimate recorded 6,327 dolphins in March 2025.
accepted.tq: Read the exact figure carefully when options contain digit transpositions.

accepted.s: The dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration generally associated with clean water is
accepted.x: A clean-water DO value is greater than 8.0 mg/L.
accepted.tq: Match the parameter with its indicative clean-water range.

accepted.s: Which parameter measures the oxygen required by bacteria to decompose organic matter?
accepted.x: Biochemical oxygen demand, or BOD, measures the oxygen needed by bacteria to decompose organic matter.
accepted.tq: Separate BOD from COD and physical water-quality measures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. COD includes oxygen needed to oxidise biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter.
2. A clean-water COD value is generally less than 5.0 mg/L.
3. BOD and COD have identical meanings and measure only biodegradable matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: COD covers biodegradable as well as non-biodegradable organic matter and its clean-water value is below 5.0 mg/L. Statement 3 is false because it incorrectly equates COD with BOD and excludes non-biodegradable matter.
accepted.tq: Use the biodegradable versus total oxidisable matter distinction.

accepted.s: A river stretch is classified as polluted when its BOD is
accepted.x: A river is considered polluted when BOD exceeds 3 mg/L; a Priority-I stretch has BOD above 30 mg/L.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general pollution threshold from the Priority-I threshold.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between suspended solids and dissolved solids in water analysis?
o: Suspended solids are retained on a filter, whereas dissolved salts pass through it.
Suspended solids pass through a filter, whereas dissolved salts are retained.
Both suspended and dissolved solids are retained on a filter.
Neither category is affected by filtration.
accepted.x: Suspended solids such as silt and clay are retained on a filter, while dissolved solids such as sodium salts pass through it.
accepted.tq: Use the filtration distinction to separate physical categories.

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only correct water-quality associations?
o: NTU—turbidity; TDS—dissolved salts; coliform count—faecal contamination
accepted.x: NTU is used for turbidity, TDS represents dissolved salts, and coliform count indicates faecal contamination.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure measurement unit and eliminate mismatched parameters.

accepted.s: For CPCB Class A water, namely a drinking-water source requiring disinfection but not conventional treatment, the total coliform limit is
accepted.x: The CPCB Class A standard specifies total coliform not exceeding 50 MPN/100 ml.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Class A total-coliform value from the bathing faecal-coliform value.

accepted.s: The bathing-water standard cited for faecal coliform in the Ganga is
accepted.x: The cited Ganga bathing standard for faecal coliform is 2,500 MPN/100 ml.
accepted.tq: Compare the bathing standard with the stricter drinking-source standard.

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the progression of trophic states in a water body?
accepted.x: The progression is oligotrophic, mesotrophic, eutrophic and, where enrichment becomes extreme, hypereutrophic.
accepted.tq: Arrange the trophic stages from low to extreme nutrient enrichment.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the causal chain in eutrophication?
o: Suspended solids → fluoride formation → algal bloom → oxygen enrichment
Nutrient depletion → algal bloom → increase in dissolved oxygen → fish kills
Algal decay → nutrient removal → oxygen enrichment → hypoxia
Nutrient enrichment → algal bloom → decomposition → depletion of dissolved oxygen
accepted.x: Nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment promotes algal blooms; decomposition of the algae consumes dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxia and fish kills.
accepted.tq: Follow the process chain from trigger to ecological consequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a trigger of eutrophication?
accepted.x: Fertiliser runoff, sewage, detergents, aquaculture effluent and airborne nitrogen can trigger eutrophication. Reduction of atmospheric nitrogen inputs is not a trigger.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed or negative form of a recognised causal factor.

accepted.s: Ritual offerings containing dairy effluent can accelerate water-quality deterioration because they may
o: Remove nitrogen and phosphorus from the water
Have high BOD and rapidly deplete dissolved oxygen
Convert all suspended solids into dissolved salts
accepted.x: Dairy effluent associated with ritual offerings can have BOD far above sewage, causing rapid depletion of dissolved oxygen.
accepted.tq: Apply the BOD–DO relationship to a specific pollution source.
